headline: Rupee Hits Seven-Month High Near ₹93.40, Squeezing IT Exporters' Earnings
subheadline: The rupee's rise to about ₹93.39–₹93.41 per dollar, powered by foreign inflows and cheaper oil, cuts the rupee value of TCS and Infosys's dollar earnings — and the Nifty IT index has fallen over 5.5% this month.
body:
• The Indian rupee climbed to around ₹93.39–₹93.41 per US dollar on November 18, its strongest level in seven months, according to Upstox.
  • The rise is a headwind for TCS, Infosys and other IT exporters: they earn most revenue in dollars and other foreign currencies but pay a large share of costs in rupees, so a stronger rupee shrinks rupee revenue and margins.
  • The benchmark Nifty IT index is down over 5.5% so far this month and has fallen for a third straight day, Upstox reported.
  • For readers sending money to India, each dollar now converts into fewer rupees than at the rupee's weakest point this year, ₹96.81 per dollar; the rupee is still about 4% weaker than on January 1, when a dollar cost ₹89.98.

The Indian rupee rose to its strongest level in seven months on Wednesday, November 18, trading around ₹93.39 to ₹93.41 per US dollar, according to Upstox. The move extends a recovery from ₹96.81 per dollar, the weakest level the currency touched earlier this year, and puts the rupee on course for its best month in 20 months, with a gain of about 1.7% so far in November.

What is driving the rupee up

Two forces are doing most of the work, Upstox reported. Foreign institutional investors have returned as net buyers of Indian equities for the first time this year, putting a net ₹94,963 crore into Indian stocks through November 17, according to NSDL data cited by Upstox. Brent crude, India's biggest import cost, has also eased to as low as $90 a barrel in recent weeks, from above $115 at the height of the US-Iran war. RTTNews likewise reported on Tuesday that the rupee had strengthened to its strongest in seven months, outperforming other Asian peers, as Indian shares closed higher on steadier oil prices and continued foreign investor inflows.

The recovery is partial. At ₹93.51, the rupee remains around 4% weaker than at the start of the year, when a dollar cost ₹89.98, Upstox noted.

Why a stronger rupee squeezes IT earnings

India's large IT services firms are exporters. TCS, Infosys and their peers earn most of their revenue in US dollars, euros and pounds, while a large share of their expenses — salaries and operations in India — is paid in rupees. When the rupee rises, the same dollar revenue converts into fewer rupees, and the shortfall lands largely on profit margins, Upstox explained.

Investors have been pricing that in. The benchmark Nifty IT index is trading lower for a third straight day and is down over 5.5% so far this month, according to Upstox. On Tuesday, information technology stocks underperformed the wider market, with Infosys, Tech Mahindra and HCL Technologies falling 1–2% as investors weighed the impact of an appreciating rupee on their revenue, RTTNews reported.

The last quarter, in two currencies

The September quarter (Q2 FY27) shows why the exchange rate matters so much to the headline numbers. TCS posted revenue from operations of ₹73,188 crore, up 11.2% year on year in rupees — but growth in constant currency, which strips out exchange-rate movements, was only 2.8%, according to company filings cited by Upstox. Infosys reported revenue of ₹49,244 crore, up 10.7% in rupees and 1.5% in constant currency. Upstox calculated that about 8 to 9 percentage points of the topline growth at both companies came from the exchange rate rather than from underlying business performance.

Profit told the same story. On a like-for-like basis that excludes a one-time charge in the year-ago quarter, TCS's net profit grew 7.6% in rupees to ₹13,884 crore, but fell 1% in dollars, to $1,450 million from $1,464 million. Infosys's net profit rose 6.2% in rupees to ₹7,823 crore, but declined 2.5% in dollars, to $817 million. Margins narrowed at both firms despite the weaker rupee's cushion: TCS's profit-after-tax margin slipped to 19.0% from 19.6% a year earlier, and Infosys's fell to 15.9% from 16.6%.

What to watch

Upstox said the rupee's recovery will depend largely on oil prices and foreign money flows: as long as both remain supportive, the rupee's rise is likely to continue. For IT companies, that would add a currency challenge on top of the AI-related pressure their share prices have already faced this year. The next test is the December quarter, the first full quarter in which a materially stronger rupee would flow through reported revenue and margins.

key_takeaways: Rupee reaches ₹93.39–₹93.41 per dollar, a seven-month high.
IT exporters face squeezed margins due to stronger rupee.
Nifty IT index down over 5.5% this month.
Foreign institutional investors have returned as net buyers.
Rupee remains about 4% weaker than January 1 levels.
